title: Bake-off: long discharge summary (heart failure)

pages.text:
SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FAKE DATA ONLY
Sampletown General Hospital - Department of Medicine
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: TESTPERSON, Robin (FAKE)        MRN: H00071234
Date of birth: 1949-11-03                Health card: 0000-000-000-ZZ
Admitted: 2026-10-14                     Discharged: 2026-10-20
Attending physician: Dr. Quinn Notreal (FAKE), General Internal Medicine
Family physician: Dr. Casey Placeholder (FAKE), Maplewood Family Health Team

Reason for admission
Mr. Testperson, a 76-year-old man, came to the emergency department with three days of
increasing shortness of breath, swelling of both ankles, and needing three pillows to sleep.
He gained about 4 kg in the week before admission. He had no chest pain and no fever.

Background
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, diagnosed in 2023.
- High blood pressure for about 20 years.
- Type 2 diabetes, managed with metformin.
- Atrial fibrillation, on apixaban.
- Osteoarthritis of both knees. He had been taking ibuprofen 400 mg up to three times a day
  for knee pain for the past month, bought without a prescription.

Medications before admission
- Furosemide 20 mg by mouth once daily
- Metoprolol 25 mg by mouth twice daily
- Ramipril 5 mg by mouth once daily
- Apixaban 5 mg by mouth twice daily
- Metformin 500 mg by mouth twice daily
- Ibuprofen 400 mg by mouth up to three times daily (over the counter)

Findings on admission
Blood pressure 156/92, heart rate 98 and irregular, oxygen saturation 89% on room air.
Crackles at both lung bases. Swelling of both legs up to the knees.
Chest X-ray: fluid in both lungs and small fluid collections around both lungs (bilateral
pleural effusions). Heart size enlarged, similar to the X-ray of 2025.
ECG: atrial fibrillation, rate 96. No new changes compared with the ECG of 2025.
Troponin: normal on two tests six hours apart. There was no heart attack.
NT-proBNP: 4,850 ng/L (on his last visit in May 2026 it was 1,210 ng/L).
Creatinine 138 umol/L on admission (his usual is about 105 umol/L); eGFR 43 mL/min/1.73m2.
Potassium 4.9 mmol/L. Sodium 134 mmol/L. Hemoglobin 128 g/L.

Hospital course
1. Heart failure flare. He was treated with furosemide 40 mg IV twice daily for three days.
   His breathing improved and he lost 5.2 kg of fluid. Oxygen was stopped on day 3.
   An echocardiogram on 2026-10-16 showed an ejection fraction of 35%, unchanged from 2024.
   The valves looked normal apart from mild leaking of the mitral valve.
   The most likely trigger was the regular ibuprofen use, which can make the body hold on to
   salt and water and can strain the kidneys.
2. Kidney function. Creatinine rose to a high of 151 umol/L on day 2, then improved to
   112 umol/L at discharge (eGFR 54). Metformin was held while in hospital and restarted at
   discharge at the same dose.
3. Atrial fibrillation. Heart rate was well controlled on metoprolol once the fluid came off.
   Apixaban was continued with no change.
4. Incidental finding. A CT scan of the chest on 2026-10-17, done to look at the fluid,
   showed a 4 mm nodule in the left lower lobe. The radiologist reported no evidence of
   malignancy and said no follow-up scan is needed for a nodule of this size in his situation.
5. Diabetes. Blood sugars ranged from 6.8 to 11.2 mmol/L. HbA1c was 7.4%.

Changes to medications at discharge
- Furosemide INCREASED from 20 mg to 40 mg by mouth once daily.
- Ibuprofen STOPPED. Do not take ibuprofen, naproxen or other anti-inflammatory pain
  medicines. Acetaminophen up to 1 g three times daily may be used for knee pain instead.
- Continue metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, ramipril 5 mg once daily, apixaban 5 mg twice
  daily and metformin 500 mg twice daily with no change.

Discharge weight: 81.4 kg.

Instructions for the patient
- Weigh yourself every morning. Call your family doctor if your weight goes up by more than
  2 kg in 3 days, or if your breathing or ankle swelling gets worse.
- Limit salt to less than 2 g of sodium a day. Limit fluids to about 1.5 to 2 litres a day.
- Blood test (creatinine, potassium) in 1 week, ordered at discharge.

Follow-up
- Family doctor, Dr. Placeholder, within 1 week.
- Heart Function Clinic, Sampletown General Hospital, in 2 weeks (2026-11-03 at 10:30).
- Cardiology will consider adding a newer heart failure medicine at the clinic visit.

Diagnoses at discharge
1. Acute decompensated heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%), most likely
   triggered by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) use.
2. Acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease, improving.
3. Atrial fibrillation, rate controlled.
4. Incidental 4 mm left lower lobe lung nodule, no follow-up required.

Electronically signed by Dr. Quinn Notreal (FAKE), MD, 2026-10-20 14:05
